items.reason: Pinning 23 refs requires resolving each tag to a commit SHA against api.github.com, and this session has no network; the repo already ships `npm run actions:pin --update`, which pins AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in one reviewable pass, so there is nothing useful to add offline.

Added two fault-injection suites that execute the degradation paths end to end — the LLM chokepoint under provider errors, exhausted retries, malformed JSON, degenerate-but-parsing output, abort and BYOM user faults; and the Google Ads sync under 500/401/403 including the halfway-through case — both blocking inside test:unit -> check:ci -> pre-push.

Added docs/task-index.md, a task-keyed routing table over every document plus every ADR by the seam it governs, nominated in .ai/manifest.yaml as guidance.taskIndex (verified by the existing blocking agents:surface gate) and held true by a new unit test that fails on a dead route, an unrouted ADR, or an entry point that stops linking to it.

Already covered: scripts/commit-subject.mjs holds a content contract (narration, first person, session-outcome, elapsed-time, placeholder rules) enforced as blocking rubric A5 by scripts/agent-review.mjs inside check:ci and pre-push, with scripts/commit-check.mjs for range audits; the only piece left is a committed .husky/commit-msg hook, and writing under .husky/ was refused as a sensitive path in this session.

lessons: This repository answers 'is the practice real?' with a script, not prose — before adding a new gate, check whether an existing blocking one already validates the shape you need (scripts/agent-surface.mjs validates every pointer listed in .ai/manifest.yaml's guidance block, so declaring a new pointer there costs one array entry instead of a new npm script, a required-checks entry and a merge-gate row).

Non-interactive Ascent sessions here cannot run node (permission is refused, not just unsandboxed) and cannot write under .husky/, so any test authored in one is unverified by construction: prefer injecting faults at a seam the source itself names as injectable (src/lib/google/ads.ts documents that global fetch is its only transport) over inferring a mock's contract, because the former is checkable by reading.

ADR-0007's rung discipline makes 'add a new blocking npm script' the expensive option; a node:test file under test-unit/ is already blocking via test:unit -> check:ci -> .husky/pre-push, needs no package.json or required-checks change, and is the house pattern for asserting wiring (see test-unit/delivery-contract.test.mjs).
